settle: A job-level link between permits and certificates that survives lot changes (DOB's own job-to-CO crosswalk), the HPD list of projects vested in 421-a with their commencement dates, and a completion horizon of six years for the 2022 cohort (2028) to see whether the 2031 extension lets vested projects wait.

research_needed.question: Which of the 807 jobs that started foundations in the six months before 15 June 2022 were vested in 421-a, and which of those have no CO?
research_needed.data: HPD 421-a(16) applications with commencement dates; DOB job numbers
research_needed.design: match on BBL and job; compare vested and non-vested starts in the same window

research_needed.question: How often does the BBL on a permit differ from the BBL on the certificate of occupancy for the same job?
research_needed.design: job-number match, then compare BBLs by cohort year

notes: Registered run: rates of no CO within 1,096 days of the first initial foundation permit, BBL matching: 2017 0.677 (n 541), 2018 0.626 (n 516), 2019 0.449 (n 497), 2020 0.310 (n 290), 2021 0.331 (n 393), 2022 0.379 (n 807), 2023 0.287 (n 366). The control windows 2017 and 2018 (0.68 and 0.63) were far above 2019 (0.45). A check after the result, by job number, showed that the registered BBL matching misses certificates for older jobs: for 2017 legacy jobs, 59% had a CO under the same job number within 36 months, against 32% found by BBL. The permit's lot and the certificate's lot differ for many older jobs, probably because lots were merged, split or converted to condominium billing lots after the permit. EXPLORATORY (analyses/stalled/vesting_exploratory.py, decides nothing): matching by job number or BBL, the 36-month no-CO rates are 2017 0.396, 2018 0.490, 2019 0.406, 2020 0.300, 2021 0.323, 2022 0.375, 2023 0.279. D1 under this matching is -0.055 (-0.096 to -0.014), so the refutation does not depend on the matching defect; legacy jobs only, D1 is -0.014 (-0.079 to 0.047). Against the 2021 window D1 is 0.052 (-0.004 to 0.108). The rush window had 807 foundation starts against about 520 a year in 2017-2019. At 48 months its no-CO rate (0.235) is within the range of 2017-2019 (0.25 to 0.30). By November 2026, 140 of the 807 rush-window jobs have no CO. The rush to pour footings before the deadline therefore added about 300 starts, most of which were completed at the usual rate; it did not produce a measurable excess of stalled foundations citywide. The 2023 window stalls less than 2022, which fits a composition change (jobs that could not vest are smaller or condominium projects) as well as the vesting account.
notes_referee: Referee reproduced D1 -0.208 under the registered rule; with job-number matching and lot-less jobs kept, -0.083 (-0.122 to -0.044). Verdict stands. Project mix changed (50+ unit jobs 28% in 2022 vs 13%); exploratory: among 50+ unit jobs the rush stalled more, +0.108 (+0.013 to +0.204). About 230 starts brought forward, not 290.
